name: Cluj-Napoca
title: Holidays in Cluj-Napoca
intro: Transylvania's lively student city, with a grand old square, a buzzing café and food scene, big summer festivals and a salt mine you can go boating in nearby. Here's what Cluj-Napoca is like, when to go and how long to stay.
image_alt: Red rooftops and colourful buildings of central Cluj-Napoca, with a domed church and green hills behind under a cloudy sky
facts_note: Cards are widely accepted, but carry a few lei for markets and small cafés. The EU is bringing in new entry checks, so check the rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: May, June and September are the best months for walking the city, with warm days and fewer crowds. July and August are warm and full of festivals, including Electric Castle and Untold, so book early. Winters are cold and often snowy, but December's Christmas market is lovely.

things.name: Piața Unirii
things.blurb: The big main square, with the Gothic St Michael's Church and a statue of King Matthias Corvinus.

things.name: Salina Turda
things.blurb: A former salt mine about 40 minutes away, with a lake and rowing boats, a Ferris wheel and an underground amusement park.

things.name: Cafés and food
things.blurb: Cluj has some of Romania's best coffee shops and restaurants, from Transylvanian stews to modern tasting menus.

things.name: Botanical Garden
things.blurb: A large garden on a hillside, with a Japanese garden, glasshouses and a Roman-style garden.

things.name: Cetățuia Hill
things.blurb: A short climb to a viewpoint over the rooftops, best at sunset.

things.name: Turda Gorge
things.blurb: A dramatic limestone gorge with a walking path along the river, close to the salt mine.

things.name: Central Park
things.blurb: A big leafy park by the river with a lake, rowing boats and the old casino building.

faqs.question: How do you get to Cluj-Napoca from the UK?
faqs.answer: Fly direct from London. Wizz Air flies from Luton and Ryanair flies from Stansted. Check the latest timetables, as routes change. The airport is about 20 minutes from the centre.

faqs.question: Is Cluj-Napoca worth visiting?
faqs.answer: Yes. It's one of Romania's liveliest cities, with good food, nightlife and festivals, and it's a great base for exploring Transylvania.

faqs.question: How many days do you need in Cluj-Napoca?
faqs.answer: Two or three days covers the city and a trip to Salina Turda and Turda Gorge. Add more if you want to explore the Apuseni Mountains.

faqs.question: When is the Untold festival?
faqs.answer: Untold is held in Cluj every summer, usually in early August. Electric Castle takes place at a castle near the city in July. Check dates, as they change each year.
